p1c1.caption: Figure I · The horizon tears
p1c1.opener_composition: Painted night star-map fills the slot (gilt constellation lines, star points, compass rose, graticule ticks — painted strokes, no engraving). A horizontal canvas tear crosses the lower third: upper flap curls up (Dim Type canvas-back, Newsprint edge, gilt stitch ticks) revealing three broadsheet column-rules beneath. Coming-apart action: the sky-map unmakes itself into print. One Signal accent max (single red star).
p1c1.palette_role: Gilt-dominant: gilt star-lines and map furniture on Night Ink; tear edges Newsprint.
p1c1.rationale: The title image is literal — the chapter closes on the crashed boat and 'a big rip' [C1:113]. Painted, not engraved, per the medium lock, so the tear reads as ruptured scenery; the columns beneath preview the book's printed-serial identity.
p1c1.reading_treatment: Stitched-patch dividers at the three-question waypoints (P70 independence / P90 nationalism / P102 Nazis — verified heads); O4 redaction of 'Somaliland' wired by supervisor book.js (match lands on intact P88 spelling; hyphenated P87 left as prose); end-seal end-torn-edge under P115.
p1c1.title: A Horizon Made of Canvas

p1c2.caption: Figure II · The cabinet of anomalies
p1c2.opener_composition: Painted curiosity cabinet on umber ground: three gilt specimen frames pinned at conflicting angles (Kenya street-corner with blue-car rectangle; Borboni gold-on-oxblood cartouche scrap; 1914 gilt encirclement arcs), overlapping, over a torn Newsprint wall-chart with a vertical rip. Exactly one Signal Red pin (top frame); other pins gilt; label plates blank. Coming-apart action: nothing sits straight; the chart behind is torn.
p1c2.palette_role: Gilt frames + Dim Type label plates on painted umber ground; one signal pin.
p1c2.rationale: The chapter is a specimen tray of historical anomalies that refuse to fit — tilted painted frames stage 'does not fit the chart' without a single engraved line. Corner Man's corner appears as place, not portrait (no figures).
p1c2.reading_treatment: Dispatch panels, quote-only per designer ruling (1-based, verified): SEWARD P59–69 + cartouche-lead P58; PROPAGANDA P96–98 + lead P95; GREY-A P102–103 + intro P101; GREY-B P109–113 + rubricated 'Grey responds' cartouche; GREY-C P115–118 + pull-line cartouche 'As he wrote in early 1916'; P104–108/114/119 stay body. O4 redaction of '443 million' (P68) wired by supervisor book.js. End-seal end-specimen-pin under P123.
p1c2.title: More Historical Anomalies

p1c3.caption: Figure III · For the King over the water
p1c3.opener_composition: The white Jacobite cockade large at optical center (painted Newsprint rosette, Oxblood heart, gilt ring) over brushworked Stuart-rose wallpaper (Oxblood ground, gilt sprigs). The lower-right corner is torn away, revealing a cracking pale timeline band with misaligned gilt ticks and one snapped tick. Coming-apart action: the timeline fails under the cockade. No Signal in plate (Oxblood heart carries the red).
p1c3.palette_role: White + gilt on painted rose-oxblood ground.
p1c3.rationale: The Jacobite chapter earns the book's own seal at full size: the cockade IS the chapter's argument (restoration as loyalty, not theory). Painted ground keeps the cohort medium pure; the torn corner stages the W-force's timeline cracking.
p1c3.reading_treatment: Sentence pull-lines per designer ruling (paras stay body): 'Doubt is a slow flower.' after P2 and 'History 1, mystery 0.' after P6, Garamond 500 + gilt side-rule, inter-para placement; duplication sanctioned as pull-quote form. NO salutation decoration (O3: plural address, verified). NO redaction (O4 budget spent c1/c2/c4). End-seal end-white-rose under P127.
p1c3.title: The Jacobite History of the World

p1c4.caption: Figure IV · The first Whig
p1c4.opener_composition: Torn painted Putney Debates broadsheet nailed to a Press Black board: Newsprint scrap with deckled edges, diagonal tear across its lower half, Oxblood column-wash (rules only, no baked text). Four gilt nail-heads, one pulled half-loose with the sheet corner lifting. Signal devil-tail fleuron at the colophon. Coming-apart action: the nailed sheet works itself free.
p1c4.palette_role: Oxblood ink on painted newsprint scrap; gilt nail-heads on dark board.
p1c4.rationale: Dr. Johnson's quip ('the first Whig was the Devil') stages as a period sheet — Putney, the Dartmouth, the Tennis Court Oath are the chapter's named scenes [C4:5–6]. The tear continues the cohort grammar to its verdict chapter.
p1c4.reading_treatment: Salutation debut: P1 mid-sentence 'dear open-minded progressive' gets the 1.1em margin cockade ONLY via supervisor book.js (no line treatment — canon §4.5). Type 1/2/3 taxonomy tablets at P23 (type 3) / P28 (type 1) / P57 (type 2) with mono headers. O4 redaction of 'St. Petersburg' (P5) wired by supervisor book.js. End-seal end-devil-tail under P82 (open-question close).
p1c4.title: Dr. Johnson's Hypothesis
